Vivek — thanks for the quick escalation. My read: Vanguard is a compelling strategic reference and the AE has a good relationship, but 45% is beyond our standard authority. I can greenlight up to 35% discount with the following constraints:
- Move to a 2-year prepaid structure (reduces long-tail exposure).

Emily — appreciate the transparency. We want to keep moving. Internal review suggests we can offer two paths that balance your need for front-loaded capacity and our finance constraints:

Option A — Accelerated 2-year prepay (preferred):
- 2-year term, 35% term discount off list.
- Year 1 prepay of the first 60% of commitment to enable the early rollout.
- Quarterly usage reconciliation and a 6-month clawback if usage < 60% of prepay.

Option B — 3-year prepay with CFO exception (requires exec approval):
- 3-year term, up to 38% discount (one-time exception) with a milestone-based credit release for the front-loaded allocation.
- Requires amended MSA and CFO sign-off.

I've attached a revised term sheet and our pricing model (redwood-pricing-model.xlsx). Let me know which direction you'd prefer; if it's Option B, I understand you'll need an explicit exec-level approval and a redline window.
